literal: Thinking 'I am a poor man', do not do evil deeds; if done, a poor man he will become again once more.
translation: Do not commit evil deeds thinking, 'I am poor.' If you do, you will only become poorer once again.
modern: நான் ஏழை என்று நினைத்துத் தீய செயல்களைச் செய்யக் கூடாது; அவ்வாறு செய்தால், மீண்டும் மேலும் வறுமை உடையவன் ஆகிவிடுவான்.
explanation: This couplet warns against using poverty as an excuse to commit wrongful or evil deeds. A person might think that because they have nothing, they are justified in resorting to bad deeds to survive. However, the poet warns that doing evil to escape poverty will only result in falling into even deeper poverty and ruin in the future. The words 'மற்றும்' and 'பெயர்த்து' emphasize the repetitive and compounding nature of this downfall, showing that evil actions inevitably multiply one's misery rather than relieving it.
